headline: Between Sep 2024 and Jan 2026 the federal civilian workforce fell 12%, and the two largest land-management agencies each lost more than a quarter of their staff: a fiscal and policy shock, not an AI effect.
suggested_chart_form: Dot plot of percentage change by unit, one row per unit, each labelled with its own period and base; lower-bound rows drawn as an open marker with an arrow; no bars, no ranking across bases; table beside the chart.
source_note: Partnership for Public Service (OPM data, to Jan 2026); Inside Climate News (OPM data, Mar 6 2026); Agri-Pulse (OPM data, Jan 21 2026). Bases differ by row and must not be compared as one series; USDA OIG reports a different USFS figure (16% in 2025) on another base. Sector-wide figures exclude Tribal, state, local, NGO and private workforces.
evidence_label: E (external sources read and verified; see source_ids per row)

headline: Most AI in federal environmental bureaus is classical machine learning for science work, and most of it is not yet deployed: 61 of the 347 use cases that report a stage are in production.
suggested_chart_form: Stacked horizontal bars by AI type (segments = development stage, Deployed first), with the 'stage not reported' segment shown hatched and labelled; table beside the chart.
source_note: OMB 2025 Federal Agency AI Use Case Inventory (README as of Apr 13 2026), environmental bureaus of USDA, DOI, DOC (NOAA) and EPA as extracted by EMST LM (docs/research/labor-market-ai-impact/scripts/omb_inventory_env.py). 'Deployed' = development_stage 'Deployed' only; OMB's README pools deployed and piloted. NOAA reported no stages. Self-reported by agencies; registration is not use.
evidence_label: E (external sources read and verified; see source_ids per row)

headline: Species detection, remote sensing, water and fire lead federal environmental AI; none of the five use cases in NEPA, environmental review or permitting is deployed.
suggested_chart_form: Horizontal bars of use cases per function family with the deployed share as a darker inner bar; families overlap (keyword-classified), so no totals row; table beside the chart.
source_note: OMB 2025 Federal Agency AI Use Case Inventory; EMST LM keyword classification of use-case names and descriptions (a use case can fall in more than one family). 'Deployed' = development_stage 'Deployed' only.
evidence_label: E (external sources read and verified; see source_ids per row)

headline: Commercial AI tools for drafting, summarizing, writing and search are licensed at 10,000 or more users in each of the three main federal environmental departments: availability at workforce scale, which is not the same as use.
suggested_chart_form: Small table (department x use-case category) with the licence band as the cell value; no chart needed. Product names are deliberately omitted.
source_note: OMB 2025 consolidated COTS AI use cases (ombegov GitHub), rows for USDA, DOI and EPA marked in use with a band of 10,000+ licences or users. Licence bands are agency estimates; they measure availability, not frequency or quality of use.
evidence_label: E (external sources read and verified; see source_ids per row)

headline: Forest plans written under the 2012 Planning Rule devote about 31% of their components to monitoring, against about 3% under the 1982 rule: a durable demand for monitoring design, evaluation and reporting.
suggested_chart_form: Paired dot plot (1982 rule vs 2012 rule) with 95% CI whiskers for the plan-equal values; component-weighted values as hollow markers; table beside the chart.
source_note: OpenLMP 0.1.0 plan components (catalog 2026-10-21, CC0), derived by EMST LM (docs/methods/scripts/wp10_lmp.py). Cross-era comparison of different plans, not a time series; about 95% of components are USDA Forest Service plans, all in western states. Headline weights each plan equally (95% CI = mean +/- 1.96 SE); component-weighted values are the sensitivity check. Mentions measure what plans name, not obligations. Tribal touchpoints are excluded pending Tribal Advisory Council review.
evidence_label: E (external sources read and verified; see source_ids per row)

source_note: OpenLMP 0.1.0 plan components (catalog 2026-10-21, CC0), derived by EMST LM (docs/methods/scripts/wp10_lmp.py). Cross-era comparison of different plans, not a time series; about 95% of components are USDA Forest Service plans, all in western states. Headline weights each plan equally (95% CI = mean +/- 1.96 SE); component-weighted values are the sensitivity check. Mentions measure what plans name, not obligations. headline: Official 2025-35 projections show analytical, engineering and technician occupations growing faster than the +3.5% all-occupation average, foresters slower, and forest and conservation workers and water operators declining.
suggested_chart_form: Dot plot of projected percentage change by occupation with a vertical reference line at +3.5%; 'about average' band of +/-1 point shaded; data scientists shown with an axis break; table beside the chart.
source_note: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Projections 2025-35 (released Aug 27 2026), Table 1.2 and Occupational Outlook Handbook pages. Projections are context, not evidence of skill change; BLS does not attribute these occupation projections to AI. The 'about average' band (+/-1 point) is an EMST display convention, not a BLS category. Wildland firefighters are not counted separately.
evidence_label: E (external sources read and verified; see source_ids per row)

headline: The entry rungs are thinning now, for fiscal and policy reasons: no non-fire seasonal hiring at the Forest Service in 2025, conservation internship postings down 44% on one board, and fewer than 8 in 100 federal employees under 30.
suggested_chart_form: Indicator table (one row per indicator, each with its own unit, period and scope) with a small inline bar for the percentage rows only; do not plot rows on a common axis.
source_note: National Parks Traveler (Nov 10 2025) on Conservation Job Board data; Partnership for Public Service (OPM data); Office of Rep. Neguse (Mar 23 2026) relaying USFS statements; Rep. Schrier et al. letter (Mar 23 2026) citing the USFS Trail Program Status Report. Each row has its own base. These are signals with fiscal and policy drivers; none is attributed to AI.
evidence_label: E (external sources read and verified; see source_ids per row)

headline: In 2025-26 policy instruments reshaped review, authorization, hiring and disclosure work faster than any technology did, and more dated changes are already scheduled for 2027.
suggested_chart_form: Horizontal timeline with one swimlane per domain; recorded events as filled markers, scheduled dates as hollow markers, pending actions as dashed markers; status labels in text, not colour alone; table beside the chart.
source_note: EMST L5 instrument registry and driver events (data/v2/instruments, data/v2/events; agent-recorded, unreviewed) filtered to events whose dates rest on verified records (V1-V4 key facts and the corrections register); scheduled and pending items from the same verified records. Litigation outcomes after the dates shown were not checked. Held (Tribal-related) instruments excluded.
evidence_label: E (external sources read and verified; see source_ids per row)

headline: EMST v2's first 13 role profiles form three corridors that cross all three crafts and end in state and federal role variants; no role yet has a change indicator that has passed EMST's evidence rule.
suggested_chart_form: Three horizontal swimlanes (one per corridor) of role boxes in step order, with levels as a band inside each box and 'emerging' roles outlined dashed; a footer row per box shows 'change indicator: none active' and the count of watch signals. No craft blends or change ratings are drawn: those are agent drafts awaiting multi-rater assessment.
source_note: EMST mvp_role_set.csv (ADR-0006, CA decision) and WP-08 generated change views (docs/build/WP-08/generated/change_view/). Indicator status is computed by the ADR-0028 evidence rule (two independent signal families, two periods, named human review); every attached signal is at watch status. Tribal variants are held and not shown.
evidence_label: Structure: CA decision (ADR-0006). Indicator status: computed. No agent ratings shown.
